pbm_regulator: Registration with the Insurance Department under Act 77 of 2024, which applies to fully insured plans.
pbm_rules: Limits on steering patients to PBM-owned pharmacies and on clawbacks; network adequacy standards; annual PBM transparency reports (first due July 1, 2026). Spread pricing is to be studied rather than banned.
pbm_recent: HB 2050 would bar PBMs from owning pharmacies; referred to House Health in November 2025 (as reported). On Oct. 13, 2026, the Attorney General announced a lawsuit against insulin manufacturers Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk and Sanofi and PBMs including Express Scripts, CVS Caremark and OptumRx in Commonwealth Court, alleging violations of the state's consumer protection law, civil conspiracy and unjust enrichment. The allegations have not been decided.
affordability_board: None. No board bill found in the 2025–26 session; earlier bills were introduced in 2019–20 and 2021–22.
contract_pharmacy_340b: No law. HB 2797, introduced Sept. 29, 2026, addresses 340B reimbursement and distribution protections; it is in House Human Services.

pbm_regulator: License from the State Corporation Commission's Bureau of Insurance (Va. Code § 38.2-3465 et seq.).
pbm_rules: Spread pricing banned for insurers and their PBMs.
pbm_recent: 2026: SB 669 and HB 830 require pass-through pricing and full rebate pass-through starting July 1, 2027. 2025: HB 2610 and SB 875 direct a single Medicaid PBM by July 1, 2026.
affordability_board: None. The legislature passed board bills in 2024, 2025 and 2026; each was vetoed (Gov. Youngkin in 2024 and 2025; Gov. Spanberger on May 19, 2026).
price_reporting: Yes, since 2021 (Va. Code § 54.1-3442.02). Manufacturers report each year on brand drugs with a list price of $100 or more and price increases of 15% or more (generics: 200% or more). Filings are confidential (Va. Code § 32.1-23.4); aggregate data is public.
contract_pharmacy_340b: No law. A 2024 bill (SB 119) was vetoed (as reported). A 2026 law (SB 278, Ch. 887) creates a 340B work group, with a report due Nov. 1, 2026.

pbm_regulator: HB 229 (2026) creates a PBM license under the Superintendent of Insurance (R.C. Chapter 3957), effective June 30, 2026, with the license required from July 1, 2027.
pbm_rules: Medicaid has used a single state PBM since October 2022 (R.C. 5167.24).
pbm_recent: HB 229 (2026) PBM licensing; PBM provisions in the 2025 budget bill, HB 96 (as reported).
affordability_board: None. HB 890 (2026) would create a board with payment limits across payers; it is in the House Insurance Committee.
contract_pharmacy_340b: No law; SB 198 and HB 276 are in committee. The 2025 budget added annual 340B reporting by covered entities (R.C. 3701.88).

pbm_regulator: Registration with the Maryland Insurance Administration (Insurance § 15-1601 et seq.).
pbm_rules: A PBM may not require use of a pharmacy it or an affiliate owns, except for specialty drugs (§ 15-1611.1); rules on affiliate reimbursement and generic pricing lists. Medicaid managed care contracts bar spread pricing.
pbm_recent: A 2025 PBM workgroup (Ch. 730) reports by Dec. 31, 2026.
affordability_board: Yes, since 2019. It can set upper payment limits for state and local government purchasers; a 2025 law (Ch. 610/611) allows wider use once two limits have been in effect for a year. It has voted limits for Jardiance and Ozempic; governments may begin applying them Jan. 1, 2027 and must after Jan. 1, 2028. The regulations are not yet listed as final.
price_reporting: No routine manufacturer price-increase reports; the affordability board identifies drugs for cost review using launch-price and price-increase thresholds.
contract_pharmacy_340b: Yes, 2024 (HB 1056, Ch. 962; effective July 1, 2024). Attorney General enforcement; $5,000 per package. A Fourth Circuit panel vacated the denial of a preliminary injunction and remanded in April 2026; the full court granted rehearing in late May, with no argument date confirmed. The law remains in effect (as reported).

pbm_regulator: License from the Insurance Commissioner (O.C.G.A. Title 33, Chapter 64).
pbm_rules: PBMs must charge state and local government plans the price paid to the pharmacy and must offer plans 100% rebate pass-through; they report payments 10% or more above or below national average acquisition cost.
pbm_recent: HB 196 (2025) sets acquisition cost plus a dispensing fee for state employee plans from 2026 (as reported). SB 91, limiting state plan contracts with PBMs that own pharmacies, did not pass (as reported).
affordability_board: None. HB 931 (2026) proposed a board with payment limits and did not pass (as reported).
contract_pharmacy_340b: No law. HB 139 (2025) would have barred manufacturer and wholesaler restrictions; it did not advance (as reported).
